records.text: Candace Owens said the Arizona Senate passed the Charlie Kirk memorial license-plate bill 16–2 and the Arizona House passed it 31–23.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: Anyway, so this goes through, and the Senate passed the bill 16–2. Then the House of Representatives also voted in favor of the bill, 31–23.

verification.notes: Officially sourced roll-call records show the House passed SB 1439 by 31-23, but the Senate vote was 16-12, not 16-2. The extracted transcript or spoken tally dropped the digit 1 from the Senate no-vote count, so the combined statement is directly contradicted.

sources.title: Votes: Arizona SB 1439, 2026
sources.relevance: Records the House vote as 31-23 and the Senate vote as 16-12, directly refuting 16-2.

records.text: Candace Owens cited the proposed law as charging $25 for the specialty plate, with $17 deposited annually into a conservative grassroots network special-plate fund.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: There's got to be money somewhere, right? There's got to be ka-ching, ka-ching somewhere. So how it actually would have worked is that you would have paid a $25 fee for that specialty plate, $17 of which would have been an annual donation deposited into a conservative grassroots network special plate fund, according to the legislation.

verification.notes: The official Arizona Senate fact sheet states that the special plate fee would be 25 dollars, consisting of an 8 dollar administration fee and a 17 dollar annual donation transmitted to the Conservative Grassroots Network Special Plate Fund.

records.text: Katie Hobbs wrote that SB 1439 fell short of bringing people together because it inserted politics into a government function that should remain nonpartisan.
records.speaker: Katie Hobbs

appearances.snippet: Sacred democratic institutions. I will continue working toward solutions and bringing people together, but this bill falls short of that standard by inserting politics into a function of government that should remain nonpartisan.

verification.notes: The transcript accurately quotes Governor Katie Hobbs's SB 1439 veto explanation. The governor's office records the veto and links the letter; contemporaneous coverage reproduces the same sentence about inserting politics into a government function that should remain nonpartisan.

records.text: Tyler Bowyer accused Katie Hobbs of vetoing the Charlie Kirk license-plate bill for political reasons after Kirk's murder.
records.speaker: Tyler Bowyer

appearances.snippet: Katie Hobbs beat up this over politics after Charlie (Charlie Kirk) was brutally murdered. Disgusting. Yeah, I'm sure you just wanted that in memorial.

verification.notes: A publicly archived embed of Tyler Bowyer's March 7, 2026 X post contains the same accusation: he wrote that Katie Hobbs vetoed the plate over politics after Charlie Kirk was murdered. The statement accurately characterizes Bowyer's public accusation without adopting it as fact.

records.text: Candace Owens said revenue from the Charlie Kirk specialty plate would go to the organization now run by his wife.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: And at the end of the day, who's that going to? Who's that money going to? It's going to his wife's organization now.

verification.notes: The official SB 1439 fact sheet directs annual fund allocations to a 501(c)(3) founded in 2012 with a high-school and college grassroots network and the stated civic mission, criteria identifying Turning Point USA. TPUSA's official team page confirms Erika Kirk is its CEO and board chair.
